title: Serve-patterns messaging by industry
content:
Purpose

Quick, tactical note for the GTM team: consolidate a small set of differentiated messaging angles for five target sectors that lean on Redwood Inference's serving-first thesis. This doc is intentionally rough and experiment-oriented. Use it to seed one-pagers, field playbook snippets, and A/B copy tests for paid channels and sales enablement.

How to use this note
- Pick 1 primary hook and 1 fallback per sector to test as a hero line in demand gen and SDR outreach.
- Capture one operational proof point (metric or capability) per sector to use in technical selling.
- Map likely competitor responses and the minimum asset we need to neutralize them.
- Open questions are at the bottom — leave quick comments with evidence or links.

High-level framing
- Core claim: Redwood makes serving predictable and cost-effective across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, letting engineering teams ship LLM features without building complex inference infra.
- Empathy for buyers: they are not buying a model; they are buying consistent behavior at scale: latency, cost predictability, data isolation, and reliability.
- Selling lever: show concrete unit economics and operational tradeoffs (tokens per minute, p95 latency, caching savings).

Notes on style and tone
- Technical but pragmatic — speak to engineers and platform leads.
- Avoid hype about model size — focus on serving behavior and outcomes.
- Use short, testable claims (numbers, e.g., 30–60% cost reduction vs naive self-hosting for customer chat loads).

Sector briefs and suggested hooks
1) Fintech (payments, neo-banks, risk scoring)
- Primary persona: Head of ML or platform, VP engineering for core products, compliance lead for regulated data flows.
- Pain we solve: unpredictable token spend, bursty traffic at end of day / market events, need for private deployments and strong auditability for regulators.
- Primary hook: Predictable inference economics for high-volume customer flows — fewer surprises on bill cycles and predictable SLOs at peak.
- Fallback hook: Dedicated pools and on-prem options that satisfy audit and data residency requirements without rewriting model code.
- Operational proof point to carry: reference case or sim: 3x throughput gains with batching + 40% token cost drop using prefix caching on customer support prompts.
- Key competitor messaging to neutralize: cloud endpoints that tout model access but lack workload-aware batching or private deployment options. Counter with: we benchmark on representative payment workloads and publish capacity profiles.
- Minimal asset: a short technical note + cost calculator spreadsheet for payment chat volumes; one pager for compliance teams.

2) Healthcare (clinical decision support, patient messaging, RCM)
- Primary persona: Head of engineering for digital health, security/compliance officer, CTO at mid-market healthtech.
- Pain we solve: data governance, audit trails, and reproducible outputs for clinical workflows. Need to run in VPC or on-prem to meet HIPAA-like controls.
- Primary hook: Private deployments with audit logs and KMS integration for PHI-sensitive inference, plus rollbackable model rollouts tied to evals.
- Fallback hook: Hosted API with strict data retention and contractually isolated tenants for pilot phase.
- Operational proof point: integration patterns for KMS + automatic request tracing that ties a model output back to a prompt and model version.
- Competitor moves: boutique healthcare ML vendors claim domain expertise; counter: we provide integration playbooks plus SLO guarantees and a path to private deployment.
- Minimal asset: compliance cheat sheet for security teams, short integration example showing KMS and audit-trail plumbing.

3) Legal (contract review, e-discovery, knowledge retrieval)
- Primary persona: Head of automation, L&D, legal ops, CTO at large law firm.
- Pain we solve: need for deterministic outputs, verifiable provenance, and fallbacks when hallucination risk is unacceptable. Also budget constraints for high-volume batch tasks.
- Primary hook: Serving controls that reduce hallucination risk via deterministic reranking and ensemble fallback policies while keeping throughput predictable.
- Fallback hook: Hybrid routing so sensitive lanes fall back to smaller models or cached answers when confidence is low.
- Operational proof point: ability to pin model versions and run A/B evals on prompt sets with automated regression alerts.
- Competitors: legal tech startups offering fine-tuned models. We respond by emphasizing serving-level guarantees and evaluation tooling that prevents regressions during deploys.
- Minimal asset: demo prompt set + evaluation report; a 1-page cheat-sheet for legal ops on risk controls.

4) Enterprise SaaS (productizing LLM features inside incumbent apps)
- Primary persona: Product lead for platform features, director of engineering, VP product.
- Pain we solve: scaling variable user features, unpredictable per-request latency harming UX, and unknown unit economics for embedding-heavy features.
- Primary hook: Plug-and-play inference that preserves product UX at scale — configurable latency SLOs and cost knobs so product teams stay within budget.
- Fallback hook: Optimize by workload: suggestions for batching, quantization, and cache policies tailored to feature patterns (search vs. chat vs. summarization).
- Operational proof point: recipe examples that reduce per-user cost for embeddings-driven search by 50% using incremental caching and smaller embedding variants for cold items.
- Competitors: cloud providers with managed endpoints but limited cost controls. Counter with clear toolset for tradeoffs and per-route cost visibility in the console.
- Minimal asset: product playbook with 3 canonical patterns + sample dashboard screenshots showing cost breakdowns.

5) Government & Defense (sensitive, classified, air-gapped needs)
- Primary persona: procurement lead, security architect, program manager for acquisition.
- Pain we solve: air-gapped deployments, FISMA-like controls, need for strict supply-chain provenance and long-term support contracts.
- Primary hook: Private deployment ISO + SCA-ready stack with HSM integration and long-term support options; evidence of secure release practices.
- Fallback hook: Dedicated region with contractual guardrails for initial pilots before full air-gapped migration.
- Operational proof point: documented on-prem installation checklist and a support SLA tailored to classified workloads.
- Competitors: large defense contractors and specialist integrators. Our edge: modular private package plus a small, nimble professional services engagement to shorten time to deploy.
- Minimal asset: installation playbook and a procurement-friendly one pager on compliance posture.

Competitive mapping (summary)
- Cloud managed endpoints: strength in model breadth and global infra; weakness in batch-aware cost controls and private deployment granularity. Messaging: emphasize serving economics and private deployment path.
- Boutique vertical model providers: strength in domain tuning; weakness in scale, SLOs, and predictable cost. Messaging: emphasize operational guarantees and rollout/eval tooling.
- Open-source self-hosted stacks: strength in control and cost at scale; weakness in time-to-productive and engineering overhead. Messaging: emphasize faster time-to-value and lower total ops burden with comparable economics.

Experiment plan and prioritization
- Week 1: Build 5 one-pagers (one per sector) and 3 short proof snippets (cost calc, KMS integration, prompt-regression example).
- Week 2: Run A/B hero copy test on email drip for fintech and enterprise-saas. Track open rate, demo request conversion, and technical-content clicks.
- Week 3: SDR script draft + objection cheat sheet for fintech and healthcare.
- Metrics: demo request rate, MQL->SQL conversion, time-to-first-pilot agreement, and engineering questions raised during trials.

Open questions and risks
- Can engineering produce reliable benchmark numbers for the fintech payment simulation by next week? See JIRA-1992.
- Need legal review on the healthcare compliance cheat sheet; what claims can we make about HIPAA compatibility in hosted mode?
- For gov/defense, confirm whether existing SOC2 + pen test artifacts are sufficient for initial procurement.

Immediate asks for collaborators
- Ravi: drop the fintech simulation numbers and a simple spreadsheet model with 3 workload slices (support chat, fraud inference, batch reconciliation).
- Liam: sketch the compliance cheat sheet for healthcare; pull any existing legal language from prior enterprise deals.
- Sofia: assemble screenshots and sample console view for the enterprise-saas playbook (cost breakdowns).

Notes to self and rough copy swatches
- Hero swatch (fintech): Predictable inference economics for high-volume payment and support flows — no surprises at settlement.
- Hero swatch (healthcare): Run PHI inference in a private footprint with auditable trails and KMS-secured keys.
- SDR opener (legal): How do you currently validate model outputs for contract review at scale? We help make that reproducible and auditable.

Appendix: quick asset checklist
- 5 sector one-pagers (technical + business hooks)
- 3 technical proof snippets (cost calculator, KMS + audit example, prompt regression sample)
- 2 sales enablement scripts (SDR openers + objections)
- 1 field playbook with rollout templates and pilot checklist

End — leave comments inline, mark action items with @assign, and we will iterate toward a first public-facing bundle for the fintech pilot in 3 weeks.
